problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a waste reduction strategy to lower the total volume of residual solid waste generated by several commercial establishments. Initially, no diversion measures are in place.

The profile of each establishment is as follows:
* For Facility A, the waste generation rate is 0.938 units per activity, and the activity level is 244.048.
* For Facility B, the waste generation rate is 2.448 units per activity, and the activity level is 164.42.
* For Facility C, the waste generation rate is 1.662 units per activity, and the activity level is 123.361.
* For Facility D, the waste generation rate is 2.238 units per activity, and the activity level is 60.952.
* For Facility E, the waste generation rate is 2.079 units per activity, and the activity level is 99.867.
* For Facility F, the waste generation rate is 2.529 units per activity, and the activity level is 60.476.
* For Facility G, the waste generation rate is 0.658 units per activity, and the activity level is 283.343.

To curtail waste, several diversion techniques are available, each with a specific diversion effectiveness:
* By deploying Technique1, waste volume is decreased by 49%
* By deploying Technique2, waste volume is decreased by 11%
* By deploying Technique3, waste volume is decreased by 47%
* By deploying Technique4, waste volume is decreased by 70%
* By deploying Technique5, waste volume is decreased by 30%
* By deploying Technique6, waste volume is decreased by 75%
* By deploying Technique7, waste volume is decreased by 61%

Implementing a technique at an establishment incurs an extra cost per unit of activity. The cost matrix for all establishment–technique pairings is provided below:

| Facility \ Technique | Technique1 | Technique2 | Technique3 | Technique4 | Technique5 | Technique6 | Technique7 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Facility A | 158.36 | 174.502 | 73.066 | 33.65 | 79.924 | 179.002 | 151.228 |
| Facility B | 179.981 | 83.463 | 195.007 | 104.279 | 104.529 | 185.619 | 108.662 |
| Facility C | 162.218 | 148.145 | 24.996 | 124.466 | 166.245 | 113.64 | 71.03 |
| Facility D | 25.213 | 135.575 | 68.234 | 124.498 | 90.962 | 141.055 | 76.794 |
| Facility E | 18.047 | 175.307 | 76.986 | 199.649 | 62.166 | 196.205 | 190.102 |
| Facility F | 24.258 | 131.127 | 79.029 | 162.208 | 139.088 | 191.03 | 37.128 |
| Facility G | 125.439 | 158.449 | 16.612 | 22.774 | 157.918 | 79.602 | 82.742 |

The task is to determine how to assign diversion techniques to each establishment (establishments may adopt multiple techniques concurrently), and it is permissible for an establishment to remain partially untreated if required.
The objective is to guarantee that the total residual waste is reduced by at least a proportion P = 0.484 of the initial volume, while minimizing the aggregate implementation cost.
